_comment: A chain: problems where a heap orders arriving events, ordered so each one is one change from an earlier one. Solve them in order, in one sitting, to see the change. heap = what sits in the heap and its key, event = what happens when the next item arrives or the top is popped, answer = what is returned and when. Drafted 2026-10-07 for the Smarkets live-coding round (Edge team: real-time event data, exchange). The spine is merge two sorted streams, then k streams with a heap, then one stream against a bounded heap, then two heaps that split or match the stream (1801 is the order book), then a heap driven by a clock.

21.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
21.event: take the smaller head, advance that list

88.title: Merge Sorted Array
88.heap: none: two pointers from the back
88.event: take the larger tail, write it at the end of nums1
88.change: arrays, and in place: fill from the back so nothing is overwritten

23.title: Merge k Sorted Lists
23.heap: (value, list index) for the head of each list
23.event: pop the smallest head, append it, push that list's next node
23.change: k lists: the heap picks the smallest head instead of a comparison

378.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
378.heap: (value, row, col) for the head of each row
378.event: pop the smallest, push the next cell in that row
378.change: the lists are rows; stop at the kth pop instead of draining

373.title: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums
373.event: pop a pair, push (i+1, j) and, when j == 0, (i, j+1)
373.change: rows are pairs of nums1[i] with nums2; push neighbours lazily instead of seeding every row

632.title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
632.heap: (value, list index, position) for the head of each list, plus the current max head
632.event: pop the min, record (min, max) if narrower, push that list's next and raise the max
632.answer: the narrowest (min, max) seen before any list runs out
632.change: track the max among heads too: the answer is the range between heap top and max, not the merged list

703.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
703.heap: min-heap of at most k values
703.event: push the new value, pop when the size is over k
703.answer: the heap top after each add
703.change: one stream, bounded heap: the top is the kth largest

1046.title: Last Stone Weight
1046.event: pop two, push the difference if not zero
1046.change: pop two push one until one is left

295.title: Find Median from Data Stream
295.heap: max-heap of the lower half, min-heap of the upper half
295.event: push to one side, move the top across to keep sizes within one
295.answer: a top, or the mean of both tops
295.change: two heaps split the stream; keep them balanced

1801.title: Number of Orders in the Backlog
1801.heap: max-heap of buys (price, amount), min-heap of sells (price, amount)
1801.event: a buy matches against the cheapest sell while sell price <= buy price; a sell matches the dearest buy while buy price >= sell price; what is left is pushed
1801.answer: total amount left in both heaps, mod 1e9+7
1801.change: the two heaps are the two sides of a book; an arrival consumes the other side's top while prices cross

2034.title: Stock Price Fluctuation
2034.heap: min-heap and max-heap of (price, timestamp), plus a dict timestamp -> latest price
2034.event: update writes the dict and pushes both heaps; a query pops while the top's price is not the dict's price for its timestamp
2034.answer: price at the latest timestamp, and the two heap tops after cleaning
2034.change: lazy deletion: an update makes old entries stale, pop them when they reach the top

239.title: Sliding Window Maximum
239.heap: max-heap of (value, index), or a deque of indices with values decreasing
239.event: push the new index; pop while the top's index is left of the window
239.answer: the top at each window end
239.change: staleness is by index, not by overwrite; a monotonic deque does it in O(n)

933.title: Number of Recent Calls
933.event: append t; pop from the front while front < t - 3000
933.change: window by time; the deque holds everything in the window so its length is the answer

1834.title: Single-Threaded CPU
1834.heap: min-heap of (duration, index) for tasks that have arrived
1834.event: when the heap is empty jump the clock to the next arrival; push every task with enqueue time <= clock; pop one and advance the clock by its duration
1834.change: arrivals are sorted by time; the heap holds what is ready, and a clock decides what has arrived

1942.title: The Number of the Smallest Unoccupied Chair
1942.heap: min-heap of free chairs, min-heap of (leave time, chair) for busy ones
1942.event: sort friends by arrival; before seating, pop every busy chair with leave <= arrival into free; seat on the smallest free chair
1942.answer: the chair the target friend gets
1942.change: two heaps: one of free resources, one of busy resources keyed by release time

2402.title: Meeting Rooms III
2402.heap: min-heap of free rooms, min-heap of (end time, room) for busy ones
2402.event: release rooms with end <= start; if none is free, pop the earliest ending room and delay the meeting to that end
2402.change: a waiting event is delayed instead of dropped, and the count per resource is the answer

621.title: Task Scheduler
621.heap: max-heap of remaining counts, plus a queue of (ready time, count) on cooldown
621.event: each tick pop the largest count, run it, requeue with ready time = now + n + 1; move queue heads back into the heap when ready
621.answer: the tick count when both are empty
621.change: a popped task goes to a cooldown queue instead of finishing; the clock ticks even when idle

1094.title: Car Pooling
1094.heap: min-heap of (drop-off, passengers) for riders on board
1094.event: trips sorted by pickup; before boarding, pop every drop-off <= pickup and free its seats; fail if seats are short
1094.change: resources are seats counted, not rooms named; a difference array does the same in O(n + max stop)
